English: Wooden Madrasa
A humble cluster of wooden structures, used for preliminary instruction and prayer by newly arrived scholars and students.
Stone Madrasa
Basic stone classrooms and prayer halls, providing a more permanent and respected center for learning and worship.
Teaching Madrasa
Simple lecture spaces and a growing community of instructors, increasingly attracting young scholars from nearby villages.
Expanded Madrasa
Multiple wings for classrooms and dormitories, with advanced instruction and a growing reputation for scholarship.
Madrasa Library
A dedicated library with rare manuscripts and scrolls, greatly enhancing the depth of study and attracting theologians from afar.
Enclosed Madrasa
A fortified madrasa with stone walls and protected gates, ensuring both the safety and prestige of the scholarly community.
Ornate Madrasa
Lavishly decorated halls, intricate calligraphy, and marble courtyards inspire awe, attracting patrons and increasing the influence of scholars.
Madrasa Courtyard
A sprawling courtyard for debate, reflection, and public lectures, making the madrasa a center of civic and religious life.
Grand Madrasa
A renowned institution of learning, with hundreds of scholars, vast libraries, and influence far beyond its walls.
Madrasa Complex
A legendary campus, home to scholars, theologians, jurists, and poets. Its influence shapes the faith, learning, and culture of the realm.
